appraisal_events.evidence: ce fut à elle seule qu'il adressa la parole pendant cette soirée et pas une seule fois à moi... il se contentait seulement... de l'attacher sur ma figure... comme si elle eût été un manuscrit difficile à déchiffrer
appraisal_events.explanation: Charlus talks animatedly with the grandmother and Mme de Villeparisis all evening but never once addresses the narrator, instead only training an investigative, scrutinizing gaze on him, a contrast the passage later makes explicit against his warmth toward the grandmother.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator is shut out of Charlus's conversation for the whole evening and reduced to an object of scrutiny rather than an interlocutor, while the grandmother is favored with warmth and attention.

ambiguities: Saint-Loup's later remark that Charlus has 'l'air de race... jusqu'au bout des ongles' is praise directed at the already-scored Charlus; it was not scored because its target is not a candidate and it carries no distinct evaluative outcome for Saint-Loup himself.

Mme de Villeparisis prompts Charlus by suggesting Mme de Sévigné's grief is 'un peu de littérature,' and Charlus flatly contradicts her ('Rien au contraire'); this reads as an intellectual disagreement within a request-and-response exchange rather than a clear personal diminishment of Villeparisis, so it was left unscored.
